sections.html:
Jeffersonville is the county seat of Clark County, Indiana, on the north bank of the Ohio River directly across from Louisville, Kentucky. The city covers 34.35 square miles at an elevation of 538 feet.

ZIP codes 47130, 47131 and 47199 serve the city, and Interstate 65 runs through it. The Big Four Bridge, converted to a pedestrian crossing and completed in 2014, links the Jeffersonville riverfront to Louisville. Annexation in 2008 added areas including Oak Park, and local names include Port Fulton, Warder Park, Big Four Station, the NoCo Arts and Cultural District and the Quartermaster Depot area.

Sellers here often explain a property by those names, so use the one that buyers recognize.

sections.h2: What is the history of Jeffersonville?
sections.html:
Jeffersonville's history starts with Fort Finney, established near the present-day Kennedy Bridge in 1786 and renamed Fort Steuben in 1791 before being abandoned in 1793. The settlement was probably named Jeffersonville around 1801, and a post office opened on September 13, 1803.

The city became the Clark County seat in 1802. Charlestown held the seat from 1812 until it returned to Jeffersonville in 1878. In 1813 and 1814, Jeffersonville was the de facto capital of the Indiana Territory.

During the Civil War the city was a gateway to the South, with Camp Joe Holt and Jefferson General Hospital, and the Quartermaster Depot supplied Union troops. In World War I the depot produced shirts on a large scale, earning the nickname America's largest shirt factory. Shipbuilding ran here for about 200 years until Jeffboat closed in 2018.

The 1930s and 1940s brought another chapter. Gambling helped the local economy recover after the flood, and the city earned the nickname Little Las Vegas.

sections.h2: What do Jeffersonville housing numbers look like?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau lists a median owner-occupied home value of $216,800 in Jeffersonville for 2020 to 2024, and 72.0% of housing units are owner-occupied. The city grew from 27,362 residents in 2000 to 44,953 in 2010 and 49,447 in 2020.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers in Jeffersonville?
sections.html:
The largest employers on a 2020 list were Greater Clark County Schools with 1,600 workers, Norton Clark Hospital with 1,500, Clark Memorial Hospital Foundation with 1,066, Heartland Payment Systems with 850 and Republic Bank and Trust of Indiana with 721.

The U.S. Census Bureau's National Processing Center is also in the city. Kitchen Kompact makes cabinetry in a converted part of the Quartermaster Depot and employs nearly 300 people, and Papa John's Pizza was founded in Jeffersonville.

The River Ridge Commerce Center sits near Charlestown on land once used by the Indiana Army Ammunition Plant.

sections.h2: What flood rules affect Jeffersonville houses?
sections.html:
Flooding is the biggest property question in Jeffersonville because of the Ohio River. The 1937 flood put about 90% of the city under water, and the city still manages floodplain development today.

The city participates in the National Flood Insurance Program. Flood maps are available at the Building Commissioner's office at 500 Quartermaster Court, and the Clark County Flood Insurance Study is dated August 31, 2012. The city's own notes cover several points a seller should know:

  • A city permit may be required for any development in the 100-year floodplain, including filling, excavation and fences.
  • If improvements or repairs exceed 50% of a building's market value, excluding land, the whole building must meet current floodplain standards.
  • The city keeps Elevation Certificates for buildings in the Special Flood Hazard Area, and they can help with insurance rates.
  • Flood insurance is mandatory for federally backed mortgages on buildings in a Special Flood Hazard Area.

The NFIP maximum for a single-family home is $250,000. Because the city holds a Level 8 Community Rating System rating, policies issued or renewed in a Special Flood Hazard Area on or after May 1, 2014 receive a 10% discount. The Building Commissioner's phone is 812-285-6412.

sections.h2: How does floodplain status change a Jeffersonville sale?
sections.html:
A house in a Special Flood Hazard Area can be harder to sell with a bank loan, because the lender will require flood insurance. That can change what a buyer is willing to pay or how fast they can close.

If you are unsure of your zone, the city has an interactive map, and the Building Commissioner can look up an elevation certificate. A homeowner who thinks a flood determination is wrong can ask FEMA for a Letter of Determination Review within 45 days.

Before you list, collect these items:

  • Your flood insurance declarations page, if you have one.
  • Any elevation certificate on file.
  • Records of past repairs and permits.
  • Notes on any past water entry.

sections.h2: Which schools and roads serve Jeffersonville?
sections.html:
Greater Clark County Schools serves the city. Schools listed for Jeffersonville include Franklin Square, Northaven, Pike and Riverside elementary schools, Parkview and River Valley middle schools, Jeffersonville High School and Sacred Heart Catholic School.

Interstate 65 gives Jeffersonville direct access to Louisville and the rest of the region, and the Big Four Bridge provides a walking route across the river. Because the city faces Louisville across the river, a buyer's commute is often part of how they judge a Jeffersonville address.

sections.h2: How does a sale close and get recorded in Clark County?
sections.html:
A deed for a Jeffersonville house is recorded at the Clark County Recorder's Office, 300 Corporate Drive, Room 102. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and documents are accepted for recording until 4:00 p.m. The phone is 812-285-6235.

The county posts these steps for deeds. The Assessor's Office in Room 104 reviews the deed, and the Auditor's Office in Room 106 transfers it. Fees are paid at both offices.

Clark County Recorder itemFee
Deeds and other instruments$25.00
Mortgages$55.00
Certified copy$5.00
Copy up to 11 by 17 inches$1.00 per page

A deed generally needs a notary acknowledgment, a prepared-by statement, a Social Security redaction affirmation, a legal description and the grantee's address. Indiana also requires a sales disclosure form, and property tax is due on May 10 and November 10.

sections.h2: What do Jeffersonville sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Jeffersonville sellers often deal with an older house in a river neighborhood, a floodplain question or a tenant in place.

  • Flood insurance cost and lender requirements.
  • Repairs that approach the 50% rule in the floodplain.
  • Inherited homes in older neighborhoods.
  • A move across the river or out of the area.

Whatever route you choose, get terms in writing. Ask who pays for title work and recording, ask whether the buyer will inspect the house, and confirm the closing date in the contract. If the house is in a floodplain, tell the buyer early, since flood insurance quotes can take time and a lender may need them before closing.

Jeffersonville's population grew from 27,362 in 2000 to 49,447 in 2020, so many homes here are far newer than the river neighborhoods. Areas annexed in 2008, including Oak Park, are newer parts of the city, and older streets tend to need more updating. Check each parcel against the flood map either way. A short list of what you know about the house, written down before you talk to any buyer, makes every conversation faster.

faqs.q: Is Jeffersonville in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Parts of it are. The city participates in the National Flood Insurance Program and publishes flood maps and an interactive map. Check your parcel with the Building Commissioner at 812-285-6412.

faqs.q: Do I need flood insurance to sell my Jeffersonville house?
faqs.a: You do not need it to sell, but a buyer with a federally backed mortgage on a building in a Special Flood Hazard Area must carry it. Expect questions about it.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Jeffersonville?
faqs.a: At the Clark County Recorder's Office, 300 Corporate Drive, Room 102. The deed is first reviewed by the Assessor and transferred by the Auditor.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Clark County?
faqs.a: The county lists $25.00 for deeds and other instruments, with fees also paid at the Auditor's office.
Greater Clark County Schools serves the city.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Jeffersonville house that has flood damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Disclose what you know and compare written offers. Cash buyers can purchase a house with damage as is.
